newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. February consumer credit data, dealers said on Monday.
Consumer credit for February is forecast to have been around US$6.7 billion compared with US$8.4 billion reported in January.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Everyone is waiting for tonight's release of the consumer credit figures for February, for fresh clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the day," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday, Tuesday/Wednesday and week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from last Friday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine-months unchanged at 6-3/16 6-1/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-5/16 6-3/16 percent.
